newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seen seeking "de minimis" rule repeal.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seen seeking "de minimis" rule repeal.

text.p: President Clinton is expected again to seek repeal of the two percent "de minimis" rule on corporate holdings of tax-exempt bonds when he proposes a fiscal 1998 budget on February 6, a bond industry official said Thursday.
But there would be some good news for the municipal bond market, which is adamantly opposed to de minimis repeal, the official said.
Clinton would delay the effective date of his proposal to the date of first action on the measure by a congressional committee, said the official, who asked not to be identified.
Currently, the Internal Revenue Service does not monitor whether a corporation has borrowed to purchase tax-exempt bonds as long as those holdings total no more than two percent.
The President sought to wipe out the safe harbor in his fiscal 1997 budget, as part of an ongoing campaign to close corporate loopholes.
His proposal, which covered all bonds purchased as of December 7, 1995, triggered a major slip in short-term muni prices.
The plan died after key House and Senate committee chairmen announced they would not back retroactive application of the provision.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association has warned that de minimis repeal "would, in reality, be nothing more than tax increases on companies, states and localities."
